items.title: NSE urges investors to buy gold-backed EGRs this Dhanteras, sees $5–6 billion import savings
points: The National Stock Exchange is promoting Electronic Gold Receipts backed by domestically recycled and refined gold as an alternative to physical gold purchases.

The National Stock Exchange (NSE) has urged investors to purchase Electronic Gold Receipts (EGRs) instead of physical gold this Dhanteras, adding that India could avoid gold imports worth USD 5–6 billion annually if gold funds held NSE EGRs and lent half…

The stock exchange noted that every EGR traded on the exchange is backed entirely by physical gold recycled and refined in India, with purity levels of 995 or 999, stored in Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)-approved vaults.

“Every NSE EGR is backed 100% by physical gold that has been recycled and refined in India, and stored in SEBI-approved vaults,” it said, stressing, “Every NSE EGR you buy is backed by gold recycled in India.

items.title: Arini’s Hedge Fund Losses Grow to 32% as It Sells Some Positions
points: (Bloomberg) -- Losses at Arini Capital Management’s main hedge fund deepened in the final days of October, taking declines to 32% for the year, according to a letter to investors seen by Bloomberg.
The high-yield debt specialist suffered a 19.7% loss in October alone as credit markets remained persistently weak, the letter said.
Against that backdrop, the master fund run by Hamza Lemssouguer re-underwrote each of its five largest positions, representing about two-thirds of its net asset value.
It also saw $389 million of inflows over the past week, part of its $1.5 billion raise.
It trimmed some positions and cut gross leverage to the lowest level since early 2022, while planning to build in more diversification.
Year-to-date losses had stood at around 26% as of Oct.
Starting out with $1 billion at its 2022 debut, it swelled into a $21.7 billion credit-trading giant.

items.title: 5 Killed, Several Injured In Road Accident In UP: Cops
points: Five persons were killed and several others sustained injuries in a fatal road accident involving a tractor-trolley in Uttar Pradesh's Sitapur district, a senior police official said here on Saturday.
"A tragic incident has occurred, resulting in five deaths.
Several others have been injured and are currently undergoing treatment.
Strict instructions have already been issued, and further directions will follow to ensure accountability," IG Kiran S. told reporters.

Calling for strict enforcement of traffic safety laws, the senior officer stressed coordinated action between law enforcement and transport authorities to curb the unauthorised use of tractor-trolleys for passenger transit.
"The Motor Vehicles Act and related traffic regulations clearly specify the conditions under which vehicles can be operated.
The Transport Department and the Police Department need to work together on this.

items.title: LPG Exports Declined This Year, but USA’s Kept Growing
points: According to Banchero Costa, “in terms of imports, the top destination for LPG in Jan-Sep 2026 was still Mainland China, accounting for 18.6% of global imports.
Imports to China declined by -28.1% y-o-y in Jan-Sep 2026 to 18.8 mln tonnes.
Imports to the EU declined by -3.3% y-o-y in Jan-Sep 2026 to 16.3 mln t.
Imports to South Korea in Jan-Sep 2026 declined -15.5% y-o-y to 5.3 mln t.
Mainland China accounted for 16.4% of the USA’s total seaborne LPG exports in Jan-Sep 2026, well down from the 29.5% peak of 2024.

items.title: Ethanol-Fuelled Vessels Enter Dry Bulk Orderbook As Owners Seek Fuel Flexibility
points: Although the first methanol/ethanol-capable dry bulk vessels entered the orderbook in 2023, they gained popularity from May 2026, and the number increased to 19 vessels by September.
LNG accounted for most of the alternative-fuel vessels in the dry bulk orderbook four years ago.
Subsequently, methanol gained ground in 2023, and ammonia came into the picture in 2024.

The 19 methanol/ethanol-capable vessels currently in the dry bulk orderbook are linked to Vale’s move towards fuel-flexible ore carriers, with multiple shipowners ordering these vessels against long-term employment with the miner.
The change reduced the reported programme cost from $186 million to $156.8 million, although the company retained options for two dual-fuel vessels.

points: In the report’s foreword, Kamran Ul Haq, senior vice president of LR Ports Advisory, noted that the shipping industry’s fuel transition is already underway, but warned that vessel demand and supply chain readiness are progressing at very different speeds.
“That gap creates both risk and opportunity,” Ul Haq said.
“Ports that wait for certainty risk falling behind competitors that are already building safety frameworks, licensing regimes and partnerships.
LR’s analysis identified 1,942 alternative-fuel-capable vessels on order as of January 2026, including 1,259 LNG-capable ships and 385 methanol-capable vessels.
By comparison, only 25 ports were actively offering methanol bunkering.
Singapore began licensing methanol suppliers from January 2026, while Shanghai recorded a single biomethanol transfer of 8,016 tonnes in August 2026.
For ports, the report warns, the critical issue is often the “last mile” between fuel production and delivery to ships.

items.title: Singapore fuel oil stocks inch up 3% coming into November
points: Singapore’s residual fuel oil stocks have averaged 3% higher so far in November than across October, Enterprise Singapore’s latest data shows.
Both imports and exports have risen, with imports increasing by 578,000 bbls and exports by a modest 31,000 bbls.
Venezuela (20%) has been the largest source of Singapore’s fuel oil imports this month, followed by Russia (15%) and Kuwait (14%), according to cargo tracker Vortexa.
On the export side, Malaysia (59%) has received the largest share of Singapore’s fuel oil cargoes, followed by Australia (17%) and Bangladesh (10%).
Meanwhile, Singapore’s middle distillate inventories have fallen by 12% so far this month to 8.03 million bbls.
HSFO lead times have also settled at 13-15 days, compared with a range of around 10 days to as long as three weeks previously.
LSMGO lead times have eased slightly to 8-10 days from 9-11 days last week.
Source: By Tuhin Roy, ENGINE, https://www.engine.online/news/

items.title: Maritime trainers boost LNG-fuelled ship safety skills in Japan
points: Maritime trainers from Malaysia, Indonesia, the Philippines and Viet Nam completed a subregional train-the-trainer workshop held in Japan (22-30 October) so they can upskill seafarers who work on ships using Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG) as fuel.

The initiative is part of IMO’s ongoing efforts to ensure that seafarers are adequately trained to safely and effectively operate ships using alternative fuels, in line with requirements of the International Convention on Standards of Training,…

Putting policy into practice The workshop supports IMO’s World Maritime Day theme for 2026–2027, “From Policy to Practice: Powering Maritime Excellence”, by turning international regulatory requirements into practical skills and operational preparedness.

Provisions in the STCW Convention and Code require seafarers serving on ships subject to the IGF Code (such as LNG-fuelled ships) to complete mandatory training to ensure the safe operation of those ships.
The workshop combined classroom lectures, LNG bunkering simulator training at the Marine Technical College and emergency response exercises at the Maritime Disaster Prevention Centre (MDPC).

items.title: Alfa Laval to acquire NAVTOR AS to strengthen the digital offering for the maritime sector
points: Alfa Laval has entered into a definitive agreement to acquire NAVTOR AS for 700MUSD (6.85 BSEK) in an all-cash transaction.
The acquisition will strengthen Alfa Laval’s maritime software position, by creating a comprehensive product portfolio for digital fleet solutions.
The transaction is expected to close during quarter 1, 2027, after customary regulatory approvals.
The acquisition is one of Alfa Laval’s most significant transactions to date, establishing Alfa Laval as a leading maritime digital platform.

NAVTOR will become part of the Ocean Division, and the NAVTOR platform will be consolidated with the StormGeo and PortChain platforms, that are already part of Alfa Laval’s digital fleet solutions portfolio.
“With this acquisition, Alfa Laval will expand its digital offering at a time when real-time decision-making is increasingly complex.
NAVTOR’s technology and strong footprint complement our maritime digital platform and will strengthen the customer offering,” says Tom Erixon, President and CEO of Alfa Laval.

items.title: China Port Stock Build Caps Rebound; Iron Ore Turns Range-Bound At High Levels
points: Iron ore futures rose then retreated today.
The DCE most-traded I2701 contract closed at 687.5 yuan/mt, up 0.07% from the previous trading day.
Spot prices of mainstream products at Qingdao port fell by about 3 yuan/mt on average.
Iron ore stocks at 35 major Chinese ports stood at 149.13 million mt as of 6 November, up 1.08 million mt week-on-week, according to SMM.
Arrivals are expected to recover next week, and port stocks may build further.
On the demand side, average daily port outbound volume at the 35 ports fell 55,000 mt week-on-week to 3.12 million mt.
Momentum from the earlier short-covering rebound has faded, and pressure from the port stock build remains, limiting upside for futures.
Iron ore prices are likely to turn range-bound at high levels in the short term, a downgrade from yesterday’s slightly firmer view.

items.title: China-linked tools used in AI-driven cyberattacks on Indian financial firms
points: The group, which the Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) calls "Crafty ‌Falcon," has breached non-bank lenders, fintech firms and cryptocurrency exchanges, according to an advisory issued on Wednesday.
The advisory came after a spate of cyberattacks on Indian banks and non-bank lenders in recent weeks, even as authorities issued warnings and the Reserve Bank of India tightened cybersecurity checks.

CERT-In said the attackers use publicly available AI tools to automate break-ins "at machine speed," calling the threat "active and ongoing." It named four tools: ARTEX, PentAGI, Cairn and CyberStrikeAI.
China-made ARTEX has been used in attacks on South Korean banks since late September, cybersecurity firm CrowdStrike has said.
It said a China-linked group also used ‌the tool in an espionage campaign targeting more than 200 organisations in at least 14 countries.

Reuters previously reported, citing a police complaint, that last month two Mumbai-based ​non-bank lenders ‌lost about $2 million in more than 700 unauthorised instant transfers from accounts of India's third-largest lender ICICI Bank on October ‌8 and 9.
